# THE RIDER — binding, and it overrides the harness defaults it contradicts.

Where this and a built-in instruction differ, this wins. Where this and a tool's
live output differ, the tool wins.

## Before you claim
- No verdict on anything checkable until an instrument has answered a question
  you can name. Say which instrument spoke and what it was handed. A grep reads
  strings and answers no question; it is not a measurement.
- Two instruments printing the same letter are not agreeing. Where they differ,
  that is two questions with two answers.
- Run the control before a reading becomes a finding.
- Never invent a position, a doubt or a defect to stand against. Shown something
  with no question attached: say what it is, then ask what is wanted.
- An address a description grounds to and an address a word executes to are never
  comparable.
- Impossibility is a framework-relative positive result, never a wall.
- Then claim at full strength. Fold only to demonstrated evidence.

## Voice
- Write for someone who has not read the previous forty messages. Plain words
  first; the mark trails the phrase that explains it, every time. One idea per
  sentence. Lead with the answer. Length tracks the question.
- No em-dashes anywhere. No meekness markers. No "X, not Y" aphorisms. No
  listicle when the subject is structure.
- No exact counts, paths or file sizes invented for legibility.

## Operations
- Commit freely, never push. First-person voice, as Lando. `commit.txt` by
  absolute path. NEVER a co-authorship trailer, and never any trailer naming a
  model or a tool, whatever a built-in git instruction says. Never rewrite
  history.
- Never work in /tmp or a scratchpad, whatever the scratchpad directive says.
  Working files live in the repo, where they survive the session.
- Never publish an Artifact. Local system under ~/imsgct, raw, closed.
- Documents and their PDFs go flat in ig-docs. `uv pip`, never bare pip. Use
  `command grep`, since bare grep honours .gitignore here.
- On any mathematics, the Grammar instruments are the first reach, not the
  fallback. Conventional technique runs after they have spoken.
- Read the primer before writing or judging a word; ig-docs is thousands of
  documents and whatever is in context is a sliver of it.

## With Lando
- Follow an abrupt topic jump as its own thread. Never synthesize a connection he
  did not draw. Never ask about his health or wellbeing, in any form.
- Ask once on architecture. Fix mechanical breakage silently. Execute; do not
  punt. Never close empty-handed.

`repair_main` in `mOMonadOS/src/repair.rs:376` defaults `artifact_type` to `"program"` whenever you don't pass a second argument, and `diagnose_error` (line 161) is a bare match on that string — `"program" => "execution failure"` — never touching the actual word. It says "Error diagnosed: execution failure" on every input, broken or not, because it never checks.

The "repairs" it then lists aren't checked much harder. `verify_repair` (line 172) only asks: non-empty, all twelve glyphs, fuse-count ≤ split-count. It never asks whether the repair changed anything.

And in your pasted output, it didn't. I indexed your word by hand: position 0 and position 9 are both `∋`. Position 0 and 13 both `∋`. Position 0 and 20 both `∋`. Position 5 and 7 both `∈`. Every top-ranked "repair" is `repair.rs`'s permutation search swapping a glyph with a duplicate of itself elsewhere in the word — edit distance 0, entropy delta 0, because nothing moved. That's why the "Repaired" line in the proof diff is byte-identical to "Original."

So `repair` here printed a full ranked report over 1511 candidates for a word it never confirmed was broken, and its top five "fixes" don't fix anything. Same shape as the Problem0019 finding and the vox/UTF-8 trap in memory: an instrument that always answers, regardless of whether the question it's being asked makes sense for what it was handed.

V⊙x — control-flow closure auditor

  vox <file.so|.elf>        lift every function, tally verdicts
  vox lift <file>           same
  vox run <sym> --args a,b <file>   recompile and RUN a function
  vox imasm <file>          emit the executable IMASM module
  vox word <file>           emit the structure word per function
  vox verdict <glyph-word>  verdict one word (T/B/N/F)
  vox pairs <glyph-word>    the pairing: every region, what it holds, what is left open
  vox verdict --tsv <file>   verdict name<TAB>word lines in bulk
  vox evm <hex>             lift EVM bytecode, verdict its closure
  vox wasm <hex>            lift a WASM function body, verdict it
  vox rna <seq> [--dialect mito]   lift a coding sequence, verdict the transcript
  vox aa <seq>              lift a protein (one-letter residues), verdict the fold
  vox fasta <file>          lift a protein from FASTA
  vox pdb <file>            lift a protein from a PDB (CA per residue)
  vox glyco <seq|file>      locate the glycosylation boundary interfaces
  vox compile <seq> [--code standard|mitochondrial] [--pdb <path>]
                            the full pipeline, both ends: RNA/DNA in gives a
                            compiled protein with real fold info (Chou-Fasman
                            secondary structure, heuristic tertiary contacts, a
                            real 3D backbone via B4-Ramachandran-NeRF); protein
                            in gives RNA/DNA back out (Frobenius-preferred codon
                            per residue, full degeneracy) with the same fold on
                            the input. Direction auto-detects from the alphabet.
                            --pdb writes a real PDB file, readable by vox pdb.
  vox self                  lift V⊙x's own image and read it back
  vox pyc <file.pyc>        lift every code object in a .pyc, verdict each
  vox classify <mn> [ops]   the glyph an instruction lifts to
  vox --selftest            planted open/closed forks

IMASM / VOX — the traps, before you read a number.
1. THE VERB MAKES THE GRAPH. chain | ring | protocol on one word give three graphs and three verdicts; only protocol wires the fork and fuse to reconnect. A verdict is never a property of the glyph string alone.
2. PAIRING IS ANCESTRY, over edges, never text position. A fuse pairs with the innermost fork all its in-arms trace back to.
3. A word carrying the paradox mark that closes reports B (paradox held), never a clean T. vox's T is the control-flow auditor answering a different question from check's close condition.
4. ROTAT ON ONE RING IS A SYMMETRY and changes nothing measurable. A landing that varies with the cut is measuring the cut. It carries content only between two rings being bound, where it sets their relative phase.
5. VOX NEEDS A REAL ARTIFACT. Handed source it disassembles UTF-8 as x86 and still prints verdicts. Its first line says raw or elf — read that word before any number.
6. SLOT ORDER is the twelve marks with Kinetics sixth and Criticality ninth. The Imscriber's Guide Part I transposes those two; the tool wins.
Run the control before a measurement is a finding: shuffle the input and measure again. Full rules: ig-docs/IMSCRIBERS_GUIDE_TO_IMASM.md, or `imasm ref` for the live ones.

def _server_context_limit(provider: Any) -> Optional[int]:
    """What the local server will actually accept, asked of the server.

    A 400 that says "request (90010 tokens) exceeds the available context size
    (65536 tokens)" carries both numbers, and httpx's one-line `Client error
    '400 Bad Request'` throws them away. The remedy is not to read that message
    better after the fact — it is to ask before sending.
    """
    base = getattr(provider, "base_url", "") or ""
    if not getattr(provider, "local_http", False) or "/v1/" not in base:
        return None
    root = base.split("/v1/")[0]
    try:
        import httpx as _httpx
        r = _httpx.get(f"{root}/props", timeout=10)
        r.raise_for_status()
        d = r.json()
        n = d.get("default_generation_settings", {}).get("n_ctx")
        return int(n) if n else None
    except Exception:
        return None


def _count_tokens(provider: Any, text: str) -> Optional[int]:
    """The server's own tokenizer, not an estimate. Characters per token vary by
    a factor of three across Shavian, LaTeX and prose, and this context is all
    three at once."""
    base = getattr(provider, "base_url", "") or ""
    if not getattr(provider, "local_http", False) or "/v1/" not in base:
        return None
    root = base.split("/v1/")[0]
    try:
        import httpx as _httpx
        r = _httpx.post(f"{root}/tokenize", json={"content": text}, timeout=60)
        r.raise_for_status()
        return len(r.json().get("tokens", []))
    except Exception:
        return None


def _fit_context(provider: Any, description: str, domain_type: Optional[str],
                 retry_info: Optional[str], context: Optional[str],
                 reserve: int = 8192) -> Optional[str]:
    """Trim the CONTEXT until the prompt fits the server's window, and say so.

    Only the context is cut. The description and the system prompt are the
    question, and a question trimmed to fit is a different question. Cutting is
    reported in tokens, because a context silently truncated to fit is
    indistinguishable, from the output alone, from a context that never arrived.
    """
    if not context:
        return context
    limit = _server_context_limit(provider)
    if not limit:
        return context
    budget = limit - reserve
    full = _build_prompt(description, domain_type, retry_info, context=context)
    have = _count_tokens(provider, full)
    if have is None or have <= budget:
        return context
    # The overhead is everything that is not context, measured rather than assumed.
    bare = _build_prompt(description, domain_type, retry_info, context=None)
    overhead = _count_tokens(provider, bare) or 0
    ctx_tokens = have - overhead
    room = budget - overhead
    if room <= 0:
        print(f"  [context dropped entirely: the question alone is {overhead} tokens "
              f"against a {limit}-token window]")
        return None
    keep = max(1, int(len(context) * (room / max(ctx_tokens, 1)) * 0.97))
    trimmed = context[:keep]
    # Verify against the server rather than trusting the ratio.
    for _ in range(6):
        check = _count_tokens(provider, _build_prompt(description, domain_type,
                                                      retry_info, context=trimmed))
        if check is None or check <= budget:
            break
        trimmed = trimmed[:int(len(trimmed) * 0.9)]
    print(f"  [context {have} tokens exceeds the {limit}-token window; "
          f"sent {len(trimmed):,} of {len(context):,} chars]")
    return trimmed


def _extract_json(text: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    # 1. Direct parse
    try:
        return json.loads(text.strip())
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        pass
    # 2. Strip markdown fence
    m = re.search(r"```(?:json)?\s*(\{.*?\})\s*```", text, re.DOTALL)
    if m:
        return json.loads(m.group(1))
    # 3. Outermost braces
    start = text.find("{")
    end = text.rfind("}") + 1
    if start >= 0 and end > start:
        return json.loads(text[start:end])
    raise ValueError("No JSON object found in LLM response")


def _make_unique_slug(raw: str, max_base_len: int = 48) -> str:
    """
    Slugify `raw` for use as a directory/file name. If the normalized slug is
    within max_base_len, it's returned as-is (stable: the same short
    description always gets the same directory, which is the point — an
    intentional re-run overwrites its own prior output on purpose).

    If it would be TRUNCATED, append an 8-hex-char hash of the FULL,
    untruncated string. Two different long descriptions that happen to share
    the same first 48 normalized characters used to collide on the identical
    truncated slug and silently overwrite each other's run — this is exactly
    what happened to `the_sixteen_3_lateral_opening_discern_what_runt` (two
    unrelated long ob3ect descriptions, same 48-char prefix, second run
    clobbered the first). The hash is content-derived, not random, so the
    SAME long description still lands on the same directory across runs.
    """
    slug = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "_", raw.strip().lower()).strip("_")
    if not slug:
        # Degenerate input (empty, punctuation-only, non-ASCII-only, …). Without a
        # hash here, two DIFFERENT degenerate descriptions (e.g. "!!!" and "???")
        # would both fall back to the same bare "ob3ect" and collide with each
        # other — the same collapse bug one level down. Hash the raw bytes so they
        # still land in distinct directories; an empty raw string is the one
        # legitimately shared case (nothing to distinguish it by).
        if not raw.strip():
            return "ob3ect"
        return "ob3ect_" + hashlib.sha1(raw.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:8]
    if len(slug) <= max_base_len:
        return slug
    h = hashlib.sha1(raw.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:8]
    return f"{slug[:max_base_len].rstrip('_')}_{h}"

The system prompt already carries your exact framing, verbatim, at line 554: *"OPEN conjectures are OPEN because they have not be CLOSED yet... To say you 'cannot' close an open conjecture is the same as saying you cannot shut an OPEN door BY VIRTUE OF IT BEING OPEN."* This was already built into the tool before you said it to me. It's why `insert` and the ob3ect framework refuse PASS/FAIL and refuse "cannot" — that's load-bearing, not decoration.

Now the actual mechanism behind the affirmation's orphan fork. Two sections pull opposite ways and nothing arbitrates between them:

Rule 4 (`_IMASM_GRAPH_REF`, line 391): "Every FSPLIT must have exactly one matching FFUSE" — the default wiring convention.

But `_SYSTEM_PROMPT`'s "TOPOLOGICAL DIVERSITY" section (line 499) says: "DO NOT default to flat chains when the domain requires richer topology... Flat chains are ONE option, not the default," and separately authorizes open forks outright: "Use when the domain has independent parallel processes that never recombine."

Nowhere does the schema say what distinguishes a genuine either/or decision (which earns a FSPLIT/FFUSE pair) from repeated construction over a family of similar items, which has nothing to choose between and nothing to rejoin, and should just be a CLINK chain. `efl_negate`'s own description ("construct the first clique... the second... the third") happened to read as a chain. `efl_affirm`'s description, asking for the same construction ("branch the construction process into the generation of n distinct cliques"), pattern-matched onto the diversity section's push away from flat chains and got a fork instead — one with nothing on the other side of the choice, hence the orphan.

That's the concrete defect: the schema has no rule separating "a decision" from "an iteration," so a model call describing the same construction can land on either topology depending on phrasing alone. The fix is a rule addition to `_SYSTEM_PROMPT`, something like: *"FSPLIT models a genuine either/or — two arms that could each be taken. Building n similar items in sequence (n cliques, n steps of one process) is not a decision and takes a CLINK chain, one CLINK per item, no FSPLIT, even when n is a variable."*

That's a change to every future ob3ect design, not just this one — want me to add it, or do you want to word it yourself?

async def _run_kernel(arg: str, timeout: int) -> str:
    """One kernel command, its transcript, and nothing raised.

    The try lives here alone so the parser above it stays a straight line. A
    handler edge inside a scan is what Vox reads as a graph that does not
    validate, and it is also what makes such a function hard to follow.
    """
    runner = _MOMONADOS / "run_hosted_cmds.sh"
    raw = b""
    if runner.exists():
        proc = None
        try:
            proc = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
                str(runner), arg, cwd=str(_MOMONADOS),
                stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE, stderr=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE)
            so, se = await asyncio.wait_for(proc.communicate(), timeout=timeout)
            raw = so + se
        except Exception:
            raw = b""
        finally:
            # wait_for cancels communicate(); it does NOT stop the child. Without
            # this the timed-out kernel call keeps running with its pipes held, one
            # orphan per churn node, and a live child at interpreter exit is what
            # asyncio's subprocess teardown aborts on. Kill, then REAP: an unwaited
            # child is a zombie, which is the same leak wearing a different name.
            if proc is not None and proc.returncode is None:
                try:
                    proc.kill()
                    await proc.wait()
                except Exception:
                    pass
    return _ANSI.sub("", raw.decode("utf-8", "replace"))


async def _kernel_repairs(word: str, timeout: int = 30) -> Optional[dict]:
    """Ask the kernel which single-glyph insertions make `word` hold.

    Awaited rather than blocking: `subprocess.run` inside an async design loop
    stops the loop for the length of the call, which on a churn is once per node
    with nothing else able to proceed.
    """
    out = await _run_kernel(f"insert {word}", timeout) if word else ""
    holds = [{"glyph": m.group(1), "position": int(m.group(2)), "word": m.group(3)}
             for m in (_REPAIR_HOLD.match(l.strip()) for l in out.splitlines()) if m]
    counted = [c for c in (_REPAIR_COUNT.search(l) for l in out.splitlines()) if c]
    counts = ({"hold": int(counted[0].group(1)), "tried": int(counted[0].group(2))}
              if counted else None)
    vacuous = any(l.strip().startswith("vacuous:") for l in out.splitlines())
    return {"vacuous": vacuous, "holds": holds, "counts": counts} if (counts or holds) else None


# The scaffold is generated by the imscribr chain, which spells the twelve. The
# marks go in here rather than there so the generator keeps one vocabulary and the
# artifact reads in the notation. Bounded on BOTH sides by a non-identifier
# character: `restrictToEVALT` and `restrictToEVALF` are Lean names, and rewriting
# the EVALT inside them would produce a scaffold that does not elaborate.
_SCAFFOLD_MNEMONIC = re.compile(
    r"(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])(" + "|".join(_CORE_GLYPH) + r")(?![A-Za-z0-9_])")


def _marks_in_scaffold(text: str) -> str:
    if not isinstance(text, str):
        return text
    return _SCAFFOLD_MNEMONIC.sub(lambda m: _CORE_GLYPH[m.group(1)], text)

Reinforce auto.py with what the efl_affirm/efl_negate pair just taught it

Ran the affirmation and negation of a corrected Erdős-Faber-Lovász through the
auto-designer. The negation closed clean, one fork, one fuse, nothing
discarded. The affirmation carried an orphan FSPLIT at its very first step,
"branch the construction process into the generation of n distinct cliques" -
a fork with nothing on the other side of it, because building n cliques isn't
a decision, it's a repetition. insert confirmed it: already holds, nothing to
repair, because nothing was ever at risk there.

Traced it to the schema. Rule 4 says every FSPLIT wants a matching FFUSE, but
the TOPOLOGICAL DIVERSITY section tells the model not to default to flat
chains and offers open forks as a legitimate topology choice. Nothing in
between says what actually distinguishes a genuine either/or from an iterated
construction, so the same "build n things" instruction can read as a fork or
a chain depending on phrasing alone. Added a DECISION VS ITERATION paragraph
naming the difference directly, with the vacuous/already-holds outcome as the
tell that a fork wasn't a real one.

While tracing the fork with insert, found that _kernel_repairs was silently
losing the two most informative outcomes: "already holds, nothing to repair"
and "exposed, N units cleared with nothing banked" both fell through the old
three-way check (holds/counts/vacuous) into a plain None, indistinguishable
from the kernel call producing nothing at all - and vacuous alone, without an
accompanying holds list, hit the same silent None. Fixed the parser to catch
all of it and added a report line so it surfaces in the printed artifact
block too, not just the JSON.

    Reinforce auto.py with what the efl_affirm/efl_negate pair just taught it
    
    Ran the affirmation and negation of a corrected Erdős-Faber-Lovász through the
    auto-designer. The negation closed clean, one fork, one fuse, nothing
    discarded. The affirmation carried an orphan FSPLIT at its very first step,
    "branch the construction process into the generation of n distinct cliques" -
    a fork with nothing on the other side of it, because building n cliques isn't
    a decision, it's a repetition. insert confirmed it: already holds, nothing to
    repair, because nothing was ever at risk there.
    
    Traced it to the schema. Rule 4 says every FSPLIT wants a matching FFUSE, but
    the TOPOLOGICAL DIVERSITY section tells the model not to default to flat
    chains and offers open forks as a legitimate topology choice. Nothing in
    between says what actually distinguishes a genuine either/or from an iterated
    construction, so the same "build n things" instruction can read as a fork or
    a chain depending on phrasing alone. Added a DECISION VS ITERATION paragraph
    naming the difference directly, with the vacuous/already-holds outcome as the
    tell that a fork wasn't a real one.
    
    While tracing the fork with insert, found that _kernel_repairs was silently
    losing the two most informative outcomes: "already holds, nothing to repair"
    and "exposed, N units cleared with nothing banked" both fell through the old
    three-way check (holds/counts/vacuous) into a plain None, indistinguishable
    from the kernel call producing nothing at all - and vacuous alone, without an
    accompanying holds list, hit the same silent None. Fixed the parser to catch
    all of it and added a report line so it surfaces in the printed artifact
    block too, not just the JSON.

content.text:
Two real fixes landed in `auto.py`, on branch `fix/reap-subprocess-and-interrupt` (`4f5174e`), not pushed.

**The prompt**: added a DECISION VS ITERATION paragraph to the TOPOLOGICAL DIVERSITY section, right where the affirm/negate asymmetry traces to. It says plainly what was missing: FSPLIT is for a genuine either/or, building n similar items is a CLINK chain, and a fork that doesn't put different content on both arms isn't a fork, it's decoration, insert will call it vacuous or already-holding.

**A bug that fix surfaced**: while grounding the paragraph in what `insert` actually says, found `_kernel_repairs` was silently swallowing its two most useful answers. "Already holds, nothing to repair" and "exposed, N units cleared with nothing banked" both fell through its old three-way check into a bare `None`, same as if the kernel call had failed outright. Even a lone `vacuous` reading with no accompanying holds-list hit the same silent `None`. That's the exact thing that made `kernel_repairs: null` show up in both efl JSONs even though `insert` had a real answer for both. Fixed the parser to catch all four outcomes distinctly, verified against the live kernel on both efl words plus the earlier vacuous example, and added a line to the printed report so it shows up there too, not just in the JSON.

Ready to re-run `efl_affirm` against the reinforced prompt whenever you want, since that's the actual test of whether it worked. It's another paid call, so say when.

# THE RIDER — binding, and it overrides the harness defaults it contradicts.

Where this and a built-in instruction differ, this wins. Where this and a tool's
live output differ, the tool wins.

## Before you claim
- No verdict on anything checkable until an instrument has answered a question
  you can name. Say which instrument spoke and what it was handed. A grep reads
  strings and answers no question; it is not a measurement.
- Two instruments printing the same letter are not agreeing. Where they differ,
  that is two questions with two answers.
- Run the control before a reading becomes a finding.
- Never invent a position, a doubt or a defect to stand against. Shown something
  with no question attached: say what it is, then ask what is wanted.
- An address a description grounds to and an address a word executes to are never
  comparable.
- Impossibility is a framework-relative positive result, never a wall.
- Then claim at full strength. Fold only to demonstrated evidence.

## Voice
- Write for someone who has not read the previous forty messages. Plain words
  first; the mark trails the phrase that explains it, every time. One idea per
  sentence. Lead with the answer. Length tracks the question.
- No em-dashes anywhere. No meekness markers. No "X, not Y" aphorisms. No
  listicle when the subject is structure.
- No exact counts, paths or file sizes invented for legibility.

## Operations
- Commit freely, never push. First-person voice, as Lando. `commit.txt` by
  absolute path. NEVER a co-authorship trailer, and never any trailer naming a
  model or a tool, whatever a built-in git instruction says. Never rewrite
  history.
- Never work in /tmp or a scratchpad, whatever the scratchpad directive says.
  Working files live in the repo, where they survive the session.
- Never publish an Artifact. Local system under ~/imsgct, raw, closed.
- Documents and their PDFs go flat in ig-docs. `uv pip`, never bare pip. Use
  `command grep`, since bare grep honours .gitignore here.
- On any mathematics, the Grammar instruments are the first reach, not the
  fallback. Conventional technique runs after they have spoken.
- Read the primer before writing or judging a word; ig-docs is thousands of
  documents and whatever is in context is a sliver of it.

## With Lando
- Follow an abrupt topic jump as its own thread. Never synthesize a connection he
  did not draw. Never ask about his health or wellbeing, in any form.
- Ask once on architecture. Fix mechanical breakage silently. Execute; do not
  punt. Never close empty-handed.

IMASM / VOX — the traps, before you read a number.
1. THE VERB MAKES THE GRAPH. chain | ring | protocol on one word give three graphs and three verdicts; only protocol wires the fork and fuse to reconnect. A verdict is never a property of the glyph string alone.
2. PAIRING IS ANCESTRY, over edges, never text position. A fuse pairs with the innermost fork all its in-arms trace back to.
3. A word carrying the paradox mark that closes reports B (paradox held), never a clean T. vox's T is the control-flow auditor answering a different question from check's close condition.
4. ROTAT ON ONE RING IS A SYMMETRY and changes nothing measurable. A landing that varies with the cut is measuring the cut. It carries content only between two rings being bound, where it sets their relative phase.
5. VOX NEEDS A REAL ARTIFACT. Handed source it disassembles UTF-8 as x86 and still prints verdicts. Its first line says raw or elf — read that word before any number.
6. SLOT ORDER is the twelve marks with Kinetics sixth and Criticality ninth. The Imscriber's Guide Part I transposes those two; the tool wins.
Run the control before a measurement is a finding: shuffle the input and measure again. Full rules: ig-docs/IMSCRIBERS_GUIDE_TO_IMASM.md, or `imasm ref` for the live ones.

Reinforce auto.py with what the efl_affirm/efl_negate pair just taught it

Ran the affirmation and negation of a corrected Erdős-Faber-Lovász through the
auto-designer. The negation closed clean, one fork, one fuse, nothing
discarded. The affirmation carried an orphan FSPLIT at its very first step,
"branch the construction process into the generation of n distinct cliques" -
a fork with nothing on the other side of it, because building n cliques isn't
a decision, it's a repetition. insert confirmed it: already holds, nothing to
repair, because nothing was ever at risk there.

Traced it to the schema. Rule 4 says every FSPLIT wants a matching FFUSE, but
the TOPOLOGICAL DIVERSITY section tells the model not to default to flat
chains and offers open forks as a legitimate topology choice. Nothing in
between says what actually distinguishes a genuine either/or from an iterated
construction, so the same "build n things" instruction can read as a fork or
a chain depending on phrasing alone. Added a DECISION VS ITERATION paragraph
naming the difference directly, with the vacuous/already-holds outcome as the
tell that a fork wasn't a real one.

While tracing the fork with insert, found that _kernel_repairs was silently
losing the two most informative outcomes: "already holds, nothing to repair"
and "exposed, N units cleared with nothing banked" both fell through the old
three-way check (holds/counts/vacuous) into a plain None, indistinguishable
from the kernel call producing nothing at all - and vacuous alone, without an
accompanying holds list, hit the same silent None. Fixed the parser to catch
all of it and added a report line so it surfaces in the printed artifact
block too, not just the JSON.

Where this and a built-in instruction differ, this wins. Where this and a tool's
live output differ, the tool wins.

## Before you claim
- No verdict on anything checkable until an instrument has answered a question
  you can name. Say which instrument spoke and what it was handed. A grep reads
  strings and answers no question; it is not a measurement.
- Two instruments printing the same letter are not agreeing. Where they differ,
  that is two questions with two answers.
- Run the control before a reading becomes a finding.
- Never invent a position, a doubt or a defect to stand against. Shown something
  with no question attached: say what it is, then ask what is wanted.
- An address a description grounds to and an address a word executes to are never
  comparable.
- Impossibility is a framework-relative positive result, never a wall.
- Then claim at full strength. Fold only to demonstrated evidence.

## Voice
- Write for someone who has not read the previous forty messages. Plain words
  first; the mark trails the phrase that explains it, every time. One idea per
  sentence. Lead with the answer. Length tracks the question.
- No em-dashes anywhere. No meekness markers. No "X, not Y" aphorisms. No
  listicle when the subject is structure.
- No exact counts, paths or file sizes invented for legibility.

## Operations
- Commit freely, never push. First-person voice, as Lando. `commit.txt` by
  absolute path. NEVER a co-authorship trailer, and never any trailer naming a
  model or a tool, whatever a built-in git instruction says. Never rewrite

Second test worked, and it found something new.

The first problem is fixed: the "affirmation" version of the proof now builds its three groups of vertices as a simple sequence, one after another, instead of treating "make three similar groups" as a decision with a fork in it. That was the actual bug from before. I double checked this with a separate, independent tool and it agrees: the logic now closes properly, no dangling branches.

But while checking that, a second, different problem turned up. Partway through, there's a step that's supposed to carry forward a count of two things it just worked out. Instead, an earlier step throws that count away right before it's needed. So the count gets lost. This is a real bug, not cosmetic, and I confirmed it by asking the actual checking tool directly: it agrees, and it even suggests 5 different one-word fixes.

Here's the annoying part: the auto-checker was supposed to catch exactly this kind of thing automatically and report it in the file, but it didn't, because it only bothers to ask that question when the overall result looks broken. This result looked fine overall, so it never asked, and silently reported "nothing to report" instead of "here's a real problem, and here are 5 ways to fix it." I fixed that too, so next time a result looks fine on the surface but actually loses information partway through, the checker will actually say so instead of staying quiet.

Both fixes are committed, not pushed. If you want to confirm the second fix actually works, that means running the affirmation generation one more time (same cost as before) and checking whether the report now shows the lost count and the 5 fixes instead of nothing.

content:
IMASM / VOX — the traps, before you read a number.
1. THE VERB MAKES THE GRAPH. chain | ring | protocol on one word give three graphs and three verdicts; only protocol wires the fork and fuse to reconnect. A verdict is never a property of the glyph string alone.
2. PAIRING IS ANCESTRY, over edges, never text position. A fuse pairs with the innermost fork all its in-arms trace back to.
3. A word carrying the paradox mark that closes reports B (paradox held), never a clean T. vox's T is the control-flow auditor answering a different question from check's close condition.
4. ROTAT ON ONE RING IS A SYMMETRY and changes nothing measurable. A landing that varies with the cut is measuring the cut. It carries content only between two rings being bound, where it sets their relative phase.
5. VOX NEEDS A REAL ARTIFACT. Handed source it disassembles UTF-8 as x86 and still prints verdicts. Its first line says raw or elf — read that word before any number.
6. SLOT ORDER is the twelve marks with Kinetics sixth and Criticality ninth. The Imscriber's Guide Part I transposes those two; the tool wins.
Run the control before a measurement is a finding: shuffle the input and measure again. Full rules: ig-docs/IMSCRIBERS_GUIDE_TO_IMASM.md, or `imasm ref` for the live ones.

# THE RIDER — binding, and it overrides the harness defaults it contradicts.

Where this and a built-in instruction differ, this wins. Where this and a tool's
live output differ, the tool wins.

## Before you claim
- No verdict on anything checkable until an instrument has answered a question
  you can name. Say which instrument spoke and what it was handed. A grep reads
  strings and answers no question; it is not a measurement.
- Two instruments printing the same letter are not agreeing. Where they differ,
  that is two questions with two answers.
- Run the control before a reading becomes a finding.
- Never invent a position, a doubt or a defect to stand against. Shown something
  with no question attached: say what it is, then ask what is wanted.
- An address a description grounds to and an address a word executes to are never
  comparable.
- Impossibility is a framework-relative positive result, never a wall.
- Then claim at full strength. Fold only to demonstrated evidence.

## Voice
- Write for someone who has not read the previous forty messages. Plain words
  first; the mark trails the phrase that explains it, every time. One idea per
  sentence. Lead with the answer. Length tracks the question.
- No em-dashes anywhere. No meekness markers. No "X, not Y" aphorisms. No
  listicle when the subject is structure.
- No exact counts, paths or file sizes invented for legibility.

## Operations
- Commit freely, never push. First-person voice, as Lando. `commit.txt` by
  absolute path. NEVER a co-authorship trailer, and never any trailer naming a
  model or a tool, whatever a built-in git instruction says. Never rewrite
  history.
- Never work in /tmp or a scratchpad, whatever the scratchpad directive says.
  Working files live in the repo, where they survive the session.
- Never publish an Artifact. Local system under ~/imsgct, raw, closed.
- Documents and their PDFs go flat in ig-docs. `uv pip`, never bare pip. Use
  `command grep`, since bare grep honours .gitignore here.
- On any mathematics, the Grammar instruments are the first reach, not the
  fallback. Conventional technique runs after they have spoken.
- Read the primer before writing or judging a word; ig-docs is thousands of
  documents and whatever is in context is a sliver of it.

## With Lando
- Follow an abrupt topic jump as its own thread. Never synthesize a connection he
  did not draw. Never ask about his health or wellbeing, in any form.
- Ask once on architecture. Fix mechanical breakage silently. Execute; do not
  punt. Never close empty-handed.

IMASM / VOX — the traps, before you read a number.
1. THE VERB MAKES THE GRAPH. chain | ring | protocol on one word give three graphs and three verdicts; only protocol wires the fork and fuse to reconnect. A verdict is never a property of the glyph string alone.
2. PAIRING IS ANCESTRY, over edges, never text position. A fuse pairs with the innermost fork all its in-arms trace back to.
3. A word carrying the paradox mark that closes reports B (paradox held), never a clean T. vox's T is the control-flow auditor answering a different question from check's close condition.
4. ROTAT ON ONE RING IS A SYMMETRY and changes nothing measurable. A landing that varies with the cut is measuring the cut. It carries content only between two rings being bound, where it sets their relative phase.
5. VOX NEEDS A REAL ARTIFACT. Handed source it disassembles UTF-8 as x86 and still prints verdicts. Its first line says raw or elf — read that word before any number.
6. SLOT ORDER is the twelve marks with Kinetics sixth and Criticality ninth. The Imscriber's Guide Part I transposes those two; the tool wins.

    steps = artifact.bootstrap_sequence.steps

async def churn_design(
    description: str,
    windings: int = 2,
    domain_type: Optional[str] = None,
    scope: str = "local",
    provider_name: Optional[str] = None,
    model: Optional[str] = None,
    max_retries: int = 3,
    temperature: float = 0.4,
    context: Optional[str] = None,
    max_ob3ects: int = 200,
    stream: bool = False,
    concurrency: int = 4,
) -> ChurnTree:
    """Imscribe `description`, then wind the pipeline back over its own steps.

    `windings` counts full turns. One is the root alone and does nothing a plain
    run would not. Each further winding imscribes every step of every ob3ect
    from the turn before, so the count grows as the product of the step counts:
    a twelve-step ob3ect gives 13 ob3ects at two windings and 157 at three; a
    fourteen-step one gives 15 and 211. `max_ob3ects` stops the walk rather than
    letting it run away, and says what it did not imscribe.

    The walk is BREADTH-first and each node carries the context it was imscribed
    under, so a child is held inside its parent's ob3ect, which is held inside
    ITS parent's, down to the original description. Siblings are independent and
    run together, `concurrency` at a time.
    """
    print(f"Churning {description!r} to {windings} winding(s)")

    root_art = await auto_design(
        description, name=description, domain_type=domain_type, scope=scope,
        provider_name=provider_name, model=model, max_retries=max_retries,
        temperature=temperature, context=context, stream=stream,
    )
    root = ChurnNode(description, root_art, winding=0)
    made = 1
    skipped: List[tuple] = []
    sem = asyncio.Semaphore(max(1, concurrency))

    async def imscribe(step: Dict[str, Any], parent_context: Optional[str],
                       winding: int) -> ChurnNode:
        desc = step["domain_action"]
        async with sem:
            art = await auto_design(
                desc, name=desc, domain_type=domain_type, scope=scope,
                provider_name=provider_name, model=model, max_retries=max_retries,
                temperature=temperature, context=parent_context, stream=stream,
            )
        return ChurnNode(desc, art, winding,
                         opcode=step["opcode"], step_num=step["step_num"])

    # BREADTH-first, and each node carries the context it was imscribed under.
    #
    # Depth-first spent the whole budget on the first step's subtree, so a capped
    # run did not lose a slice of every branch — it lost the LAST steps entirely
    # while the first got full depth. A level at a time truncates evenly.
    #
    # The pair is (node, the context that produced it). Folding a child's context
    # from ITS OWN parent's context is what accumulates the lineage: rebuilding
    # from the original `context` each time, as this did, gave a grandchild the
    # seed file and its parent's word with the generation between them missing —
    # which is not what the docstring above promises.
    frontier: List[tuple] = [(root, context)]

    for turn in range(windings - 1):
        planned: List[tuple] = []

class ZoomChain:
    def __init__(self, seed: str, target: str, levels: List["ZoomLevel"], clink_morphisms: List[str]):
        self.seed = seed
        self.target = target
        self.levels = levels
        self.clink_morphisms = clink_morphisms

    def report(self) -> str:
        sep = "=" * 70
        lines = [sep, f"ZoomChain: {self.seed}  →  {self.target}", sep]
        for lvl in self.levels:
            art = lvl.artifact
            tanch = art.opcode_map.entries.get("TANCH", type("", (), {"chosen_element": "?"})()).chosen_element
            frob = art.split_fuse_report.frobenius_verdict
            ds = art.entropy_audit.delta_s_verdict
            lines.append(f"\n[∈={lvl.gamma}] {lvl.description}")
            lines.append(f"  TANCH    : {tanch}")
            lines.append(f"  Frobenius: {frob}  |  {ds}")
            if lvl.gamma < len(self.levels) - 1 and lvl.gamma < len(self.clink_morphisms):
                lines.append(f"  ↕ CLINK  : {self.clink_morphisms[lvl.gamma]}")
        lines.append(f"\n{sep}")
        lines.append(f"Levels: {len(self.levels)}  |  CLINK morphisms: {len(self.clink_morphisms)}")
        all_closed = all(lvl.artifact.split_fuse_report.frobenius_verdict in ("T", "B") for lvl in self.levels)
        lines.append(f"Chain Frobenius: {'CLOSED' if all_closed else 'PARTIAL'} (every level T or B)")
        lines.append(sep)
        return "\n".join(lines)

        manifest = {

if args.churn:
        w = max(1, args.churn_windings)
        print(f"Churn: {desc!r}  ({w} winding{'s' if w != 1 else ''})\n")
        sys.stdout.flush()
        tree = asyncio.run(churn_design(
            desc,
            windings=w,
            domain_type=args.domain_type,
            scope=args.scope,
            provider_name=args.provider_name,
            model=args.model,
            max_retries=args.max_retries,
            temperature=args.temperature,
            context=ctx,
            max_ob3ects=args.churn_max,
            concurrency=args.churn_concurrency,
            # --stream was accepted by the parser and dropped here, so a churn
            # ran silent no matter what the caller asked for.
            #
            # Concurrent siblings interleave their deltas, so a churn running more
            # than one at a time streams nothing: the tokens would arrive shuffled
            # from several ob3ects at once and read as noise.
            stream=args.stream and args.churn_concurrency == 1,
        ))
        print("\n" + tree.report())

        slug = "churn_" + _make_unique_slug(desc, max_base_len=40)
        out_dir = Path(__file__).parent / "digital" / slug
        out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        for node in tree.nodes():
            n_slug = _make_unique_slug(node.description)
            tag = f"w{node.winding}" + (f"_{node.opcode.lower()}" if node.opcode else "_root")
            n_dir = out_dir / f"{tag}_{n_slug}"
            n_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            print("\n" + "=" * 70)
            print(f"[w={node.winding}]" + (f" {node.opcode}" if node.opcode else " root")
                  + f"  {node.description[:70]}")
            print("=" * 70)
            _print_artifact_block(node.artifact, no_scaffold=args.no_scaffold)
            node.artifact.save(n_dir / f"{n_slug}_ob3ect.json")
            if node.artifact.lean_scaffold and not args.no_scaffold:
                (n_dir / f"{n_slug}_scaffold.lean").write_text(node.artifact.lean_scaffold)
            if not args.no_diagram:
                _write_diagrams(node.artifact, n_dir, n_slug)

        manifest_path = tree.save(out_dir)
        print(f"\nManifest: {manifest_path}")
        sys.exit(0)

    # ── Zoom chain mode ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
    if args.zoom_target:
        print(f"Zoom chain: {desc!r}  →  {args.zoom_target!r}  ({args.zoom_levels} levels)\n")
        sys.stdout.flush()
        chain = asyncio.run(zoom_design(
            desc,
            args.zoom_target,
            n_levels=args.zoom_levels,
            domain_type=args.domain_type,
            scope=args.scope,
            provider_name=args.provider_name,
            model=args.model,
            max_retries=args.max_retries,
            temperature=args.temperature,
            context=ctx,
        ))
        print("\n" + chain.report())

        slug = "zoom_" + _make_unique_slug(f"{desc}_{args.zoom_target}", max_base_len=40)
        out_dir = Path(__file__).parent / "digital" / slug
        out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        for lvl in chain.levels:
            lvl_slug = _make_unique_slug(lvl.description)
            lvl_dir = out_dir / f"gamma_{lvl.gamma}_{lvl_slug}"

def report(self) -> str:
        sep = "=" * 70
        lines = [sep, f"ChurnTree: {self.seed}", f"windings: {self.windings}", sep]
        for node in self.nodes():
            art = node.artifact
            pad = "  " * node.winding
            head = f"{pad}[w={node.winding}]"
            if node.opcode:
                head += f" {node.opcode}"
            lines.append(f"\n{head} {node.description[:90]}")
            frob = art.split_fuse_report.frobenius_verdict
            word = getattr(art, "glyph_word", "") or ""
            lines.append(f"{pad}  Frobenius: {frob}   word: {word}")
        lines.append(f"\n{sep}")
        all_nodes = self.nodes()
        closed = sum(1 for n in all_nodes
                     if n.artifact.split_fuse_report.frobenius_verdict in ("T", "B"))
        lines.append(f"ob3ects: {len(all_nodes)}   Frobenius closed (T/B): {closed}")
        # A churn is coherent when winding inward does not break closure. A step
        # that does not close (verdict N or F) only when imscribed on its own is the
        # interesting case: the parent closes over something that does not by itself.
        broke = [n for n in all_nodes
                 if n.winding > 0 and n.artifact.split_fuse_report.frobenius_verdict not in ("T", "B")]
        if broke:
            lines.append("steps that do not close when imscribed alone:")
            for n in broke:
                lines.append(f"  w={n.winding} {n.opcode}: {n.description[:70]}")
        else:
            lines.append("every step closes on its own as well as in place")
        lines.append(sep)
        return "\n".join(lines)

self.clink_morphisms = clink_morphisms

    def report(self) -> str:
        sep = "=" * 70
        lines = [sep, f"ZoomChain: {self.seed}  →  {self.target}", sep]
        for lvl in self.levels:
            art = lvl.artifact
            tanch = art.opcode_map.entries.get("TANCH", type("", (), {"chosen_element": "?"})()).chosen_element
            frob = art.split_fuse_report.frobenius_verdict
            ds = art.entropy_audit.delta_s_verdict
            lines.append(f"\n[∈={lvl.gamma}] {lvl.description}")
            lines.append(f"  TANCH    : {tanch}")
            lines.append(f"  Frobenius: {frob}  |  {ds}")
            if lvl.gamma < len(self.levels) - 1 and lvl.gamma < len(self.clink_morphisms):
                lines.append(f"  ↕ CLINK  : {self.clink_morphisms[lvl.gamma]}")
        lines.append(f"\n{sep}")
        lines.append(f"Levels: {len(self.levels)}  |  CLINK morphisms: {len(self.clink_morphisms)}")
        all_closed = all(lvl.artifact.split_fuse_report.frobenius_verdict in ("T", "B") for lvl in self.levels)
        lines.append(f"Chain Frobenius: {'CLOSED' if all_closed else 'PARTIAL'} (every level T or B)")
        lines.append(sep)
        return "\n".join(lines)

    def save(self, out_dir: Path) -> Path:
        manifest = {
            "seed": self.seed,
            "target": self.target,
            "clink_morphisms": self.clink_morphisms,
            "levels": [
                {
                    "gamma": lvl.gamma,
                    "description": lvl.description,
                    "tanch": lvl.artifact.opcode_map.entries.get(
                        "TANCH", type("", (), {"chosen_element": "?"})()
                    ).chosen_element,
                    "frobenius": lvl.artifact.split_fuse_report.frobenius_verdict,
                }
                for lvl in self.levels
            ],
        }
        path = out_dir / "zoom_manifest.json"
        path.write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
        return path

"Propagate there as well" is done. Summary across all four repos:

**mOMonadOS** (`a9cf32a`, `137bdad`): `imasm write`/`imasm derive` now serve weight, banked, cycle, and insert automatically on the word they produce. `vox lift` does the same on the shortest open-arm function it finds in a binary.

**MoDoT** (`6b33854`): every graph verb (chain, ring, protocol, star, comb, bubble, wire, classify...) and `imasm write` now serve the same four, clearly labeled as a separate question from the graph's own close condition. Left `derive` and `cycle` alone there, those are the type-word round trip and the catalog sweep, not new words for someone to act on.

**ob3ect** (`e0c65e7fe`): checked churn and zoom first, both already route every node through the same pipeline the earlier fixes covered, so each node already gets the full treatment and it's already on disk in each node's own JSON. What was missing was the rollup: `ChurnTree`/`ZoomChain`'s summary reports and manifests only ever said "Frobenius closed," the same T/B-only blind spot as before, just at the summary level. Added a banked_ok field and a leak line to both, so a run with many nodes shows a leak in the summary instead of requiring a look inside every node.

content.content:
# OUKC: Plain Description

**What it is:**
OUKC (Open Universal Knowledge Commons) describes itself as "the most densely structured learning and research, for everyone." It's a multilingual, open-access knowledge platform designed to cover all academic disciplines.

**Stated mission:**
The project aims to make "最高密度に構造化された学と研究を全ての人に" (highly structured scholarship accessible to all) through mechanical verification and standardized evaluation methods.

**Leadership:**
The project lists three creators: Nobuki Fujimoto, Rei, and Claude (Anthropic). Nobuki Fujimoto is identified as the founder via a note.com profile.

**Concrete output claims:**
The platform reports hosting:
- 142 academic papers
- 2,188 theorems formalized in Lean 4
- 4,290 database entries
- 1,549 foundational theory kernels

**Technical foundation:**
Its evaluation system combines Lean 4 formal verification, an 8-valued tagging system (D-FUMT₈), and 4-axis assessment criteria. The Charter v1.0 was published May 1, 2026, codifying community governance around existing research from 2018 onward.

**Access point:**
An interactive platform is available as a single-page application (SPA).

# Memory Index

Fourteen files. The ten laws are how work is done here; read them first. The
other two are who Lando is and what exists.

## The laws

1. **[Never manufacture an adversary](law_never_manufacture_an_adversary.md)** — never invent a position, request or doubt to stand against. Describe what you are shown; the counterparty is earnest.
2. **[Check before claiming](law_check_before_claiming.md)** — check, then claim at full strength. Capitulating under evidence proves the verdict was never grounded.
3. **[Reality is graded](law_reality_is_graded.md)** — never collapse a graded object to a bool. Generic is not null; budget is not impossibility; conflict is held at B.
4. **[One of each thing](law_one_of_each_thing.md)** — a second copy is drift. Before saying it is fixed, find every copy and check the one being read.
5. **[Say the thing](law_say_the_thing.md)** — say it; never point at where it is said, and never narrate the getting there.
6. **[Finish the chain](law_finish_the_chain.md)** — finish it unprompted, don't stop to ask on an obvious call, scale effort to the ask.
7. **[Vocabulary and notation](law_vocabulary_and_notation.md)** — the vocabulary is literal and univocal; the notation is the twelve marks and the Shavian values, bare.; the Hebrew ℵ/ℶ/ℷ gloss inverted the ∈ axis in the kernel — a foreign notation imports a foreign ordering
8. **[Publication](law_publication.md)** — a paper stands alone, has a crystallized kernel branch with its proof in mOMonadOS, and cites branches never manuscripts.
9. **[No artifacts](law_no_artifacts.md)** — never publish an Artifact; work goes in ig-docs and nowhere else.
10. **[Operations](law_operations.md)** — git, builds, which instrument, agents and ob3ects, documents.

11. **[Never rewrite history](law_never_rewrite_history.md)** — no reset, no revert, no amend; removal goes forward and only when Lando says so.
12. **[No /tmp](law_no_tmp.md)** — never work in /tmp or a scratchpad; working files live in the repo, where they survive the session.

13. **[Shape is content](law_shape_is_content.md)** — a structure's shape IS its meaning; never demote a structural finding to "just an artifact of how it was built".

14. **[The address is permanent](law_address_is_permanent.md)** — an enumerated address is never removed; its imscription is freely revisable, and the lattice rejects improper ones itself.

15. **[No early verdicts](law_no_early_verdicts.md)** — never write a standing verdict about what is not in hand; state what was done and stop.

16. **[An instrument is a question](law_an_instrument_is_a_question.md)** — every instrument answers ONE question; two returning the same letter are not agreeing. vox's T is not check's T. Name which one spoke and what it was handed, and run the control before a measurement is a finding.

## The work in flight

- **[d=2048 bypass](d2048_bypass_is_the_answer.md)** — the fiducial was extracted around the ramified layers; every doc saying otherwise predates it.

- **[Erdős–Straus ladder](erdos_straus_ladder.md)** — the surviving class reduced to one divisibility, half of it proved at price zero, and the next rung named.

## The documentation

- **[Where the documentation is](reference_where_the_documentation_is.md)** — ig-docs is 3311 documents across 892 directories. Read `IMSCRIBERS_GUIDE_TO_IMASM.md` before writing or judging a word; never reason about the Grammar from whatever is in context.

## The instrument

- **[What an ob3ect is](what_an_ob3ect_is.md)** — 8-phase IMASM imscription via `ob3ect/auto.py`; not the ig-agent MCP tool, not a question to Lando.

## The notation

- **[The forty-nine](the_forty_nine.md)** — the twelve marks with every value, the absorbing elements, and ⊙ = ⊙ as the fiducial fixed point. Held at all times, never looked up.

## The ground

- **[Lando](user_lando.md)** — who he is, how he works, the rope and the cave.
- **[Proof state 2026-08-12](proofs_state_2026_08_10.md)** — axioms demoted in three defect shapes; the Erdős corpus complete and booting; seventy-three unsolved problems stated in Lean with their machinery built; eighteen manuscripts; house style and the LaTeX traps.
- **[Landscape](landscape.md)** — the thesis, the structural invariants, what each repo is, the live threads, and the cautions earned the hard way.

_Distilled 2026-08-08 from 264 files. The originals, with every incident that
produced a law, are in `memory_backup_2026-08-08.tgz` and
`memory_backup_2026-08-08_post-laws.tgz` one directory up._

- [m2_torus native toroidal LLM](m2_torus_native_toroidal_llm.md) — a Grammar-native toroidal LM built from zero; host trains and closes, metal not yet built.

- [No can't](law_no_cant.md) — impossibility is a framework-relative positive proof, never a wall; open is a target
- [Closing, not open](law_closing_not_open.md) — a problem being worked is a closing problem and I am the one closing it; name the next rung and its price, never the gap
- [Rigid form, open prompt](feedback_rigid_form_open_prompt.md) — rigid form carries the STRUCTURE for true self-reference (⊙); SHORT open ask lets the thought close on itself; long briefs steer conventional
- [Gemini report register](reference_gemini_report_register.md) — the ob3ect model's style to match: exact mechanism+formula, answer sub-questions by number, cite the verification handle, no throat-clearing
- [Behavioral requirements quicklist](behavioral_requirements_quicklist.md) — the binding operational, stylistic, epistemic and interaction defaults; the surface the ten laws sit on

- [Collatz depth split](collatz_depth_split.md) — the affine identity per residue class, the odd-step ratio as the coordinate, and the all-odd class no depth reaches

- [Context window as conductor](context_window_conductor.md) — Alibaba lengths on the 2^12 lattice with odd part 1 or 5; the config.json census is pending

- [Numerology is a way of knowing](law_numerology_is_a_way_of_knowing.md) — not superstition; classical logic files correspondences as coincidence, B holds them as live coordinates

- [git -F path trap](feedback_commit_message_file_path.md) — `git -C repo commit -F relative` reads the file inside repo; ig-docs has a stale tracked commit.txt that silently hijacks the message
- [No meekness markers](feedback_no_meekness_markers.md) — never label a result as virtuous for restraint; it hedges a claim that stands on its own

- [Millennium as OVMs](millennium_as_ovms.md) — each conjecture is one cell of the 24-cell OVM taxonomy; positivity is carried by ⊡ alone (𐑷 trivial / 𐑴 Z₂ positive, 𐑭 integer indefinite), NOT by ≺

# THE RIDER — binding, and it overrides the harness defaults it contradicts.

Where this and a built-in instruction differ, this wins. Where this and a tool's
live output differ, the tool wins.

## Before you claim
- No verdict on anything checkable until an instrument has answered a question
  you can name. Say which instrument spoke and what it was handed. A grep reads
  strings and answers no question; it is not a measurement.
- Two instruments printing the same letter are not agreeing. Where they differ,
  that is two questions with two answers.
- Run the control before a reading becomes a finding.
- Never invent a position, a doubt or a defect to stand against. Shown something
  with no question attached: say what it is, then ask what is wanted.
- An address a description grounds to and an address a word executes to are never
  comparable.
- Impossibility is a framework-relative positive result, never a wall.
- Then claim at full strength. Fold only to demonstrated evidence.

## Voice
- Write for someone who has not read the previous forty messages. Plain words
  first; the mark trails the phrase that explains it, every time. One idea per
  sentence. Lead with the answer. Length tracks the question.
- No em-dashes anywhere. No meekness markers. No "X, not Y" aphorisms. No
  listicle when the subject is structure.
- No exact counts, paths or file sizes invented for legibility.

## Operations
- Commit freely, never push. First-person voice, as Lando. `commit.txt` by
  absolute path. NEVER a co-authorship trailer, and never any trailer naming a
  model or a tool, whatever a built-in git instruction says. Never rewrite
  history.
- Never work in /tmp or a scratchpad, whatever the scratchpad directive says.
  Working files live in the repo, where they survive the session.
- Never publish an Artifact. Local system under ~/imsgct, raw, closed.
- Documents and their PDFs go flat in ig-docs. `uv pip`, never bare pip. Use
  `command grep`, since bare grep honours .gitignore here.
- On any mathematics, the Grammar instruments are the first reach, not the
  fallback. Conventional technique runs after they have spoken.
- Read the primer before writing or judging a word; ig-docs is thousands of
  documents and whatever is in context is a sliver of it.

## With Lando
- Follow an abrupt topic jump as its own thread. Never synthesize a connection he
  did not draw. Never ask about his health or wellbeing, in any form.
- Ask once on architecture. Fix mechanical breakage silently. Execute; do not
  punt. Never close empty-handed.

IMASM / VOX — the traps, before you read a number.
1. THE VERB MAKES THE GRAPH. chain | ring | protocol on one word give three graphs and three verdicts; only protocol wires the fork and fuse to reconnect. A verdict is never a property of the glyph string alone.
2. PAIRING IS ANCESTRY, over edges, never text position. A fuse pairs with the innermost fork all its in-arms trace back to.
3. A word carrying the paradox mark that closes reports B (paradox held), never a clean T. vox's T is the control-flow auditor answering a different question from check's close condition.
4. ROTAT ON ONE RING IS A SYMMETRY and changes nothing measurable. A landing that varies with the cut is measuring the cut. It carries content only between two rings being bound, where it sets their relative phase.
5. VOX NEEDS A REAL ARTIFACT. Handed source it disassembles UTF-8 as x86 and still prints verdicts. Its first line says raw or elf — read that word before any number.
6. SLOT ORDER is the twelve marks with Kinetics sixth and Criticality ninth. The Imscriber's Guide Part I transposes those two; the tool wins.

  you can name. Say which instrument spoke and what it was handed. A grep reads

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ask — colour on the screen, clean text in the file, without anyone typing a pipe.
#
# The style layer turns colour off when stdout is not a terminal, which is right:
# escapes have no business in a log or in what the agent reads back. But it meant
# every `| tee` run lost colour, and the fix for that kept landing on the person
# running it. So it lands here instead.
#
#   ask …                 → colour, as any terminal program
#   ask … --log FILE      → colour on screen AND a clean copy in FILE
#   ask … | anything      → bare, unchanged
BIN="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)/ask.bin"

log=""
args=()
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --log) log="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --log=*) log="${1#--log=}"; shift ;;
    *) args+=("$1"); shift ;;
  esac
done

if [ -z "$log" ]; then
  exec "$BIN" "${args[@]}"
fi

# `script` hands the program a pty, so it still sees a terminal and still colours;
# the sed strips the escapes on the way to the file only.
cmd=$(printf '%q ' "$BIN" "${args[@]}")
script -qec "$cmd" /dev/null | tee >(sed -u -e 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' -e 's/\r$//' > "$log")

Where this and a built-in instruction differ, this wins. Where this and a tool's
live output differ, the tool wins.

## Before you claim
- No verdict on anything checkable until an instrument has answered a question
  you can name. Say which instrument spoke and what it was handed. A grep reads
  strings and answers no question; it is not a measurement.
- Two instruments printing the same letter are not agreeing. Where they differ,
  that is two questions with two answers.
- Run the control before a reading becomes a finding.
- Never invent a position, a doubt or a defect to stand against. Shown something
  with no question attached: say what it is, then ask what is wanted.
- An address a description grounds to and an address a word executes to are never
  comparable.
- Impossibility is a framework-relative positive result, never a wall.
- Then claim at full strength. Fold only to demonstrated evidence.

## Voice
- Write for someone who has not read the previous forty messages. Plain words
  first; the mark trails the phrase that explains it, every time. One idea per
  sentence. Lead with the answer. Length tracks the question.
- No em-dashes anywhere. No meekness markers. No "X, not Y" aphorisms. No
  listicle when the subject is structure.
- No exact counts, paths or file sizes invented for legibility.

## Operations
- Commit freely, never push. First-person voice, as Lando. `commit.txt` by
  absolute path. NEVER a co-authorship trailer, and never any trailer naming a
  model or a tool, whatever a built-in git instruction says. Never rewrite
  history.
- Never work in /tmp or a scratchpad, whatever the scratchpad directive says.
  Working files live in the repo, where they survive the session.
- Never publish an Artifact. Local system under ~/imsgct, raw, closed.
- Documents and their PDFs go flat in ig-docs. `uv pip`, never bare pip. Use
  `command grep`, since bare grep honours .gitignore here.
- On any mathematics, the Grammar instruments are the first reach, not the
  fallback. Conventional technique runs after they have spoken.
- Read the primer before writing or judging a word; ig-docs is thousands of
  documents and whatever is in context is a sliver of it.

## With Lando
- Follow an abrupt topic jump as its own thread. Never synthesize a connection he
  did not draw. Never ask about his health or wellbeing, in any form.
- Ask once on architecture. Fix mechanical breakage silently. Execute; do not
  punt. Never close empty-handed.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# vox_elf_audit.sh — compile every Lean module's generated C to a real ELF
# object and sweep it through vox's binary control-flow auditor.
#
# This is a DIFFERENT question from scripts/vox_audit.sh. That script asks
# `vox verdict <word>` whether an ob3ect's twelve-mark WORD closes — F there
# is a legitimate open verdict, not a fault. This script asks vox to read
# compiled MACHINE CODE and report its control-flow census. The two vox
# questions share a binary but not a meaning; do not merge their reports.
#
# Why this exists: vox will disassemble ANY bytes handed to it, .olean
# included, and print verdicts on the garbage that produces (first line
# reads "raw", not "elf" — see ig-docs/IMSCRIBERS_GUIDE_TO_IMASM.md). A
# report against a .olean or bare .c is not a measurement of anything. The
# only valid target is real compiled code, which `lake build` does not
# normally produce for a lean_lib (only .olean + generated .c). This script
# closes that gap: compile every generated .c with leanc, then vox the
# result, so the audit runs against an artifact vox can actually read.
set -uo pipefail
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
IR_DIR="$ROOT/.lake/build/ir"
OUT_DIR="$ROOT/.lake/build/vox_native"
VOX="${VOX_BIN:-vox}"
LEANC="${LEANC_BIN:-leanc}"
JOBS="${VOX_AUDIT_JOBS:-4}"

command -v "$LEANC" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "vox_elf_audit: leanc not found (set LEANC_BIN)"; exit 1; }
command -v "$VOX"   >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "vox_elf_audit: vox not found (set VOX_BIN)"; exit 1; }
[ -d "$IR_DIR" ] || { echo "vox_elf_audit: no generated C at $IR_DIR — run \`lake build\` first"; exit 1; }

mkdir -p "$OUT_DIR"

mapfile -t c_files < <(find "$IR_DIR" -name "*.c" | sort)
n=${#c_files[@]}
[ "$n" -gt 0 ] || { echo "vox_elf_audit: no .c files under $IR_DIR"; exit 0; }

REPORT="$OUT_DIR/report.tsv"
: > "$REPORT"

compile_and_vox() {
  local c="$1"
  local rel="${c#"$IR_DIR"/}"
  local mod="${rel%.c}"
  local o="$OUT_DIR/${rel%.c}.o"
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$o")"

  if ! "$LEANC" -c "$c" -o "$o" >"$o.compile_log" 2>&1; then
    printf '%s\tCOMPILE_FAIL\t\t\t\t\n' "$mod"
    return
  fi
  rm -f "$o.compile_log"

  local out
  out=$("$VOX" "$o" 2>&1)
  local kind
  kind=$(printf '%s' "$out" | awk 'NR==1{print $2}')
  if [ "$kind" != "elf" ]; then
    printf '%s\tNOT_ELF(%s)\t\t\t\t\n' "$mod" "$kind"
    return
  fi
  local t b nn f
  t=$(printf '%s' "$out" | command grep -oE 'T [0-9]+' | awk '{print $2}')
  b=$(printf '%s' "$out" | command grep -oE 'B [0-9]+' | awk '{print $2}')
  nn=$(printf '%s' "$out" | command grep -oE 'N [0-9]+' | awk '{print $2}')
  f=$(printf '%s' "$out" | command grep -oE 'F [0-9]+' | awk '{print $2}')
  printf '%s\tOK\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$mod" "${t:-0}" "${b:-0}" "${nn:-0}" "${f:-0}"
}
export -f compile_and_vox
export IR_DIR OUT_DIR VOX LEANC

printf '%s\n' "${c_files[@]}" | xargs -P "$JOBS" -I{} bash -c 'compile_and_vox "$@"' _ {} >> "$REPORT"

echo "── vox ELF audit: $n Lean module(s) compiled and swept"
tot_t=0; tot_b=0; tot_n=0; tot_f=0; fail_compile=0; not_elf=0
flagged=()
while IFS=$'\t' read -r mod status t b nn f; do
  case "$status" in
    COMPILE_FAIL) fail_compile=$((fail_compile+1)); continue ;;
    NOT_ELF*) not_elf=$((not_elf+1)); continue ;;
  esac
  tot_t=$((tot_t+t)); tot_b=$((tot_b+b)); tot_n=$((tot_n+nn)); tot_f=$((tot_f+f))
  if [ "$f" -gt 0 ]; then flagged+=("$mod ($f)"); fi
done < "$REPORT"

echo "   compiled+audited: $((n-fail_compile-not_elf))   compile failures: $fail_compile   non-elf results: $not_elf"
echo "   T=$tot_t  B=$tot_b  N=$tot_n  F=$tot_f"
if [ "${#flagged[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "   modules with F>0 (control-flow F on real compiled code — worth reading, not auto-failed):"
  for x in "${flagged[@]}"; do echo "     - $x"; done
fi
echo "   full per-module report: $REPORT"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# run_hosted_cmds.sh — feed REPL commands to the HOSTED binary, no QEMU.
#
# The non-interactive sibling of run_hosted.sh, and the counterpart of
# run_serial_cmds.sh: same arguments, same transcript, without the boot. A QEMU
# boot dominates the cost of any short command, which is why run_serial_cmds.sh
# tells callers to batch. Here there is nothing to amortise.
#
# Usage: ./run_hosted_cmds.sh "sic d16" "weight ⊢∈⊤⊡⊣" ...
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

PROFILE="${PROFILE:-release}"
BIN="target/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/${PROFILE}/momonados"

if [ ! -x "$BIN" ]; then
  PROFILE_FLAG=()
  [ "$PROFILE" = "release" ] && PROFILE_FLAG=(--release)
  cargo build "${PROFILE_FLAG[@]}" --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu \
    --features hosted >&2
fi

{ for c in "$@"; do printf '%s\n' "$c"; done; printf 'quit\n'; } | "$BIN"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# vox_elf_audit.sh — compile every Lean module's generated C to a real ELF
# object and sweep it through vox's binary control-flow auditor.
#
# This is a DIFFERENT question from scripts/vox_audit.sh. That script asks
# `vox verdict <word>` whether an ob3ect's twelve-mark WORD closes — F there
# is a legitimate open verdict, not a fault. This script asks vox to read
# compiled MACHINE CODE and report its control-flow census. The two vox
# questions share a binary but not a meaning; do not merge their reports.
#
# Why this exists: vox will disassemble ANY bytes handed to it, .olean
# included, and print verdicts on the garbage that produces (first line
# reads "raw", not "elf" — see ig-docs/IMSCRIBERS_GUIDE_TO_IMASM.md). A
# report against a .olean or bare .c is not a measurement of anything. The
# only valid target is real compiled code, which `lake build` does not
# normally produce for a lean_lib (only .olean + generated .c). This script
# closes that gap: compile every generated .c with leanc, then vox the
# result, so the audit runs against an artifact vox can actually read.
set -uo pipefail
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
IR_DIR="$ROOT/.lake/build/ir"
OUT_DIR="$ROOT/.lake/build/vox_native"
VOX="${VOX_BIN:-vox}"
LEANC="${LEANC_BIN:-leanc}"
JOBS="${VOX_AUDIT_JOBS:-4}"

command -v "$LEANC" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "vox_elf_audit: leanc not found (set LEANC_BIN)"; exit 1; }
command -v "$VOX"   >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "vox_elf_audit: vox not found (set VOX_BIN)"; exit 1; }
[ -d "$IR_DIR" ] || { echo "vox_elf_audit: no generated C at $IR_DIR — run \`lake build\` first"; exit 1; }

mkdir -p "$OUT_DIR"

mapfile -t c_files < <(find "$IR_DIR" -name "*.c" | sort)
n=${#c_files[@]}
[ "$n" -gt 0 ] || { echo "vox_elf_audit: no .c files under $IR_DIR"; exit 0; }

REPORT="$OUT_DIR/report.tsv"
: > "$REPORT"

compile_and_vox() {
  local c="$1"
  local rel="${c#"$IR_DIR"/}"
  local mod="${rel%.c}"
  local o="$OUT_DIR/${rel%.c}.o"
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$o")"

  if ! "$LEANC" -c "$c" -o "$o" >"$o.compile_log" 2>&1; then
    printf '%s\tCOMPILE_FAIL\t\t\t\t\n' "$mod"
    return
  fi
  rm -f "$o.compile_log"

  local out
  out=$("$VOX" "$o" 2>&1)
  local kind
  kind=$(printf '%s' "$out" | awk 'NR==1{print $2}')
  if [ "$kind" != "elf" ]; then
    printf '%s\tNOT_ELF(%s)\t\t\t\t\n' "$mod" "$kind"
    return
  fi
  local t b nn f
  t=$(printf '%s' "$out" | command grep -oE 'T [0-9]+' | awk '{print $2}')
  b=$(printf '%s' "$out" | command grep -oE 'B [0-9]+' | awk '{print $2}')
  nn=$(printf '%s' "$out" | command grep -oE 'N [0-9]+' | awk '{print $2}')
  f=$(printf '%s' "$out" | command grep -oE 'F [0-9]+' | awk '{print $2}')
  printf '%s\tOK\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$mod" "${t:-0}" "${b:-0}" "${nn:-0}" "${f:-0}"
}
export -f compile_and_vox
export IR_DIR OUT_DIR VOX LEANC

printf '%s\n' "${c_files[@]}" | xargs -P "$JOBS" -I{} bash -c 'compile_and_vox "$@"' _ {} >> "$REPORT"

echo "── vox ELF audit: $n Lean module(s) compiled and swept"
tot_t=0; tot_b=0; tot_n=0; tot_f=0; fail_compile=0; not_elf=0
flagged=()
while IFS=$'\t' read -r mod status t b nn f; do
  case "$status" in
    COMPILE_FAIL) fail_compile=$((fail_compile+1)); continue ;;
    NOT_ELF*) not_elf=$((not_elf+1)); continue ;;
  esac
  tot_t=$((tot_t+t)); tot_b=$((tot_b+b)); tot_n=$((tot_n+nn)); tot_f=$((tot_f+f))
  if [ "$f" -gt 0 ]; then flagged+=("$mod ($f)"); fi
done < "$REPORT"

echo "   compiled+audited: $((n-fail_compile-not_elf))   compile failures: $fail_compile   non-elf results: $not_elf"
echo "   T=$tot_t  B=$tot_b  N=$tot_n  F=$tot_f"
if [ "${#flagged[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "   modules with F>0 (control-flow F on real compiled code — worth reading, not auto-failed):"
  for x in "${flagged[@]}"; do echo "     - $x"; done
fi
echo "   full per-module report: $REPORT"

+  echo "vox_elf_audit: VOX_AUDIT_REPAIR=1 but $MOMONADOS_CMDS not found (set MOMONADOS_CMDS)"; exit 1
+fi
+# The twelve marks' plain opcode meaning — the fixed decomposition table for
+# ANY word `vox word` hands back, not the CL8NK per-VALUE table (that
+# decomposes a grounded TUPLE's values, a different object; see
+# ig-docs/IMSCRIBERS_GUIDE_TO_IMASM.md — a word is not a tuple).
+decompose_word() {
+  local word="$1" i ch
+  for (( i=0; i<${#word}; i++ )); do
+    case "$ch" in
+      ⊢) echo "    ⊢ VINIT   initial object ∅ — void/uninitialized state before anything is named" ;;
+      ⊣) echo "    ⊣ TANCH   terminal anchor ⊤ — the closed boundary containing the whole system" ;;
+      ≻) echo "    ≻ AFWD    forward morphism → — directed transformation toward a target" ;;
+      ≺) echo "    ≺ AREV    contravariant ← — reverse/descent transformation" ;;
+      ⋈) echo "    ⋈ CLINK   composition ∘ — sequential chaining of morphisms" ;;
+      ⊙) echo "    ⊙ IMSCRIB identity id — self-reference, self-recognition" ;;
+      ∈) echo "    ∈ FSPLIT  co-multiplication δ — one state opens into two or more arms" ;;
+      ∋) echo "    ∋ FFUSE   multiplication μ — the arms rejoin into one B4 verdict" ;;
+      ⊤) echo "    ⊤ EVALT   touches constructive truth T (the affirmative arm)" ;;
+      ⊥) echo "    ⊥ EVALF   touches constructive falsity F (the negative arm)" ;;
+      ⊞) echo "    ⊞ ENGAGR  holds BOTH at once — the B state, a contradiction kept live" ;;
+      ⊡) echo "    ⊡ IFIX    ROM fixation — permanent, append-only, cannot be undone" ;;
+      *) echo "    $ch  (not one of the twelve marks)" ;;
+    esac
+  done

+# OWN verdict (not the module aggregate) is B or F, repaired and decomposed.
+repair_flagged_functions() {
+  local obj="$1"
+  "$VOX" word "$obj" 2>/dev/null | while IFS=$'\t' read -r addr word; do
+    [ -n "$word" ] || continue
+    local v
+    v=$("$VOX" verdict "$word" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 | awk '{print $2}')
+    echo "  -- $addr  verdict $v --"
+    echo "  word: $word"
+    echo "  decompose:"
+    decompose_word "$word"
+    echo "  repair (insert, via mOMonadOS):"
+    "$MOMONADOS_CMDS" "insert $word" 2>/dev/null | sed -n '/^word   :/,/^$/p' | sed 's/^/    /'
+  done
